title_en: The defeat and the promised victory of the Rum
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The Rum have been defeated, in the nearest land, and after their defeat they will themselves be victorious, in several years.
The command belongs to God before and after; on that day the believers will rejoice in God's help.
God helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.
It is the promise of God; God does not break His promise, but most people do not know.
They know an outward part of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that the Rum have been defeated in the nearest land and will be victorious after their defeat, in several years [c1]. They add that the command belongs to God before and after, and that God does not break His promise [c2][c4].
chapters.body_md:
The Rum have been defeated, in the nearest land, and after their defeat they will themselves be victorious, in several years [c1]. The command belongs to God before and after; on that day the believers will rejoice in God's help [c2].

God helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful [c3]. It is the promise of God; God does not break His promise, but most people do not know [c4]. They know an outward part of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat speak of the past and of the future: a defeat that has happened and a victory that will follow it [c1]. The Arabic for nearest land can also be read as the lowest land, and the draft keeps it open [c1]. The final ayat turn from the event to people's knowledge, saying they know the outward part of this life and are heedless of the Hereafter [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat say that the Rum had been defeated but would win after some years [c1]. They say that God keeps His promise, though most people do not know it [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places an event under God's command, before and after it [c2]. Another is that it sets the outward knowledge of this life beside heedlessness of the Hereafter [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which battle or war is meant, who defeated the Rum, where the nearest land was, or when the defeat happened.
- Not established: how many years several covers, or in what event the victory came; the ayat give only several years.
- Not established: what the believers rejoiced at beyond God's help, or what the connection of the believers to the Rum was.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the Rum with the Byzantines, of their opponents with the Persians, and the places and years of the war.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, and early historical reports on the war and on the believers' reaction. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the Byzantines, the Persians and the dating of the defeat and the victory.

The vowel reading of the verbs in 30:2-3 (defeated, will be victorious) is disputed in the readings tradition; a scholar of qira'at should decide how the page words it. The draft follows the common reading.
The phrase 'on that day the believers will rejoice' (30:4-5) is rendered closely and left open as to its cause.
